skill.name: prompt-repetition
skill.description: Applies prompt repetition guidance and Python helper logic to improve lightweight LLM accuracy on context, multiple-choice, and position lookup tasks.
skill.summary: Repeat prompts safely for lightweight models to improve accuracy on selected task types.
skill.author: supercent-io

security_audit.summary: All static findings were reviewed in context and adjudicated as false positives. The alerts come from Markdown code fences, inline examples, reference links, dictionary keys, and multiple-choice sample text. No prompt injection, credential access, command execution, or runtime network behavior was found.

static_findings.snippet: | Options-First MCQ | `A. B. C. D.` choices first | 2× | +15-40%p |
| With CoT | `step by step`, `think through` | **0×** (not applied) | ~0% |
1. **Use markers**: Detect already-applied prompts with `<!-- prompt-repetition-applied -->` marker
2. **Pass metadata**: Pass `x-prompt-repetition-applied: true` header between agents
1. **No padding substitution**: Increasing length with `.` etc. has no effect (per research)
- [Prompt Repetition Improves Non-Reasoning LLMs (Leviathan et al., 2025)](https://arxiv.org/)
- [Re-Reading Improves Reasoning in LLMs (Xu et al., 2024)](https://arxiv.org/)

content.value_statement: Lightweight models can miss context when questions arrive after important information. This skill repeats suitable prompts with guardrails to improve accuracy on selected tasks.
actual_capabilities: Identifies lightweight model families where prompt repetition is intended to apply.
Recommends two repetitions for general context and options-first question tasks.
Recommends three repetitions for position, slot, index, row, or column lookup tasks.
Skips repetition when chain-of-thought cue phrases are present.
Checks estimated token usage against a configurable context window ratio.
Provides Python helper logic for transforming prompts and wrapping LLM calls.
limitations: It increases input tokens and can raise request cost.
It does not improve every model, task, or benchmark.
It uses approximate token estimates, not provider tokenizers.
It should not be used for irreversible tool actions without review.

use_cases.title: Tune lightweight assistant prompts
use_cases.description: Improve short-answer prompts for Haiku, Flash, or mini models when key context appears before the question.

use_cases.title: Improve retrieval-style product flows
use_cases.description: Apply repetition to catalog, inventory, or documentation lookups that ask about a specific slot or position.

use_cases.title: Compare prompt variants in evaluation runs
use_cases.description: Run baseline and repeated prompts side by side to measure accuracy, cost, and latency changes.

prompt_templates.title: Repeat a simple prompt
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner use on a lightweight model.
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply prompt repetition to this lightweight-model prompt. Keep the original wording. Use two repetitions unless a stronger rule applies. Prompt: [paste prompt]

prompt_templates.title: Improve an options-first question
prompt_templates.scenario: Multiple-choice prompts where answers appear before the question.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this options-first question for prompt repetition. Tell me whether two repetitions are suitable and explain the token cost. Prompt: [paste prompt]

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a position lookup task
prompt_templates.scenario: Index, slot, row, or column tasks.
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this position lookup prompt. Decide whether three repetitions are suitable and flag any context-window concerns. Prompt: [paste prompt]

prompt_templates.title: Integrate repetition in an agent pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan prompt repetition for my agent pipeline. Include model targeting, marker handling, token limits, skip rules, and evaluation metrics. Context: [describe pipeline]

output_examples.input: Options appear before the question for a Claude Haiku task.
output_examples.output: Use two repetitions. The repeated second pass can attend to both the choices and the final question.

output_examples.input: A Gemini Flash prompt asks which item appears in slot 25.
output_examples.output: Use three repetitions if the token budget allows it. Position tasks are the strongest target for this technique.

output_examples.input: A prompt asks the model to think step by step before answering.
output_examples.output: Skip repetition. Chain-of-thought cues are excluded because the expected benefit is low.

best_practices: Use prompt repetition first on lightweight models and position-sensitive tasks.
Check token budget before applying repetition to long prompts.
Add an applied marker so multi-agent systems do not repeat the same prompt twice.
anti_patterns: Do not apply repetition to reasoning models by default.
Do not combine repetition with chain-of-thought prompting unless testing proves value.
Do not repeat prompts that request irreversible tool actions without human review.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It repeats suitable prompts so lightweight models can reprocess context before answering.

faq.question: Which models are the main targets?
faq.answer: The guidance targets Haiku, Gemini Flash, GPT-4o mini, and similar lightweight models.

faq.question: Does it change the model architecture?
faq.answer: No. It is a prompt transformation technique, not a model architecture change.

faq.question: Will it increase cost?
faq.answer: Yes. It increases input tokens, so teams should measure accuracy gains against added cost.

faq.question: When should I skip it?
faq.answer: Skip it for chain-of-thought prompts, very long prompts, and reasoning models unless evaluation supports it.

faq.question: Does it call external services?
faq.answer: No. The included logic transforms prompt text locally and documentation links only cite research references.
